chips.question: When may you drive past a school bus with flashing red lights on a divided highway?
chips.answer: Most states simply say you must stop for a school bus with flashing red lights, often from either direction. A few write the rule only for some roads: Louisiana for undivided roads, Florida for two-way roads, South Carolina for two-lane roads. In Ohio, traffic from both directions stops on roads with fewer than 4 lanes. New Jersey's rule covers 2-lane roads and multi-lane roads divided only by lines. In Washington, the rule covers drivers going the same way as the bus.

chips.question: Which states let you turn left on red onto a one-way street?
chips.answer: In most states you may turn left on red from a one-way street onto another one-way street, after stopping and yielding. A few states, including Kansas, Michigan, Idaho and Washington, also allow a left on red onto a one-way street from a two-way street. Alaska allows it except onto a two-way street, and in South Dakota only cities that pass a local rule allow it. The District of Columbia bans left turns on red. A sign forbidding the turn always wins.

chips.question: When may you pass another car on the right in most states?
chips.answer: In most states, you may pass on the right when the car ahead is making or about to make a left turn. Many states also let you pass on the right on a road with 2 or more lanes going your way. Some add one-way streets, like California and Florida. West Virginia is strictest: you may pass on the right only where a lane is marked for passing. Many states also say you can never leave the pavement to do it, like Oklahoma and Wyoming.

chips.question: Which states ban wearing headphones while driving?
chips.answer: Some states ban headphones while you drive, full stop, like Alaska, Florida, Georgia, Rhode Island and Washington. Many others ban them in both ears, so one ear is allowed, like California, Colorado, Louisiana, Minnesota and Wisconsin. Illinois and Pennsylvania allow one earpiece only for phone calls. chips.question: ¿Hay algún estado donde un pasajero pueda tener una cerveza abierta en un auto en marcha?
chips.answer: Sí, pero solo en algunos vehículos especiales, no en un carro normal. En Florida, el pasajero puede tenerla en un vehículo que lleva gente por pago o en una casa rodante. En Kentucky también se permite al pasajero en autobuses, taxis, limusinas y casas rodantes. En Nevada se permite en la parte donde se vive de una casa rodante, y en autobuses, limusinas o taxis. En un carro normal, la mayoría de los estados prohíben un envase abierto donde se sientan las personas, también al pasajero.

chips.question: Which state counts an old drunk-driving conviction against you for the most years?

chips.question: Which state suspends your license after the fewest points?
